title: Characterizing circulating tumor cells using affinity-based microfluidic capture and AFM-based biomechanics
protocol: Bring the cleaned PDMS chips into contact with APTES-silanized glass slides at 23°C and under atmospheric pressure.
Gently press on the PDMS chips to ensure surfaces are well-bonded.
Keep the AFM-Chips in a vacuum desiccator for 15 minutes.
Pipette droplets of PBS on the inlet and outlet ports of the AFM-Chips to prevent liquid evaporation during incubation.
Manually flush AFM-Chip channels with 100 μL PBS using syringes after incubations to remove unbound molecules/antibodies.
Prepare a 3 mg/mL solution of BMPS in PBS in a glass vial.
Mix the BMPS solution for 5 s using a vortex mixer.
Fill a glass syringe with 100 μL BMPS solution (3 mg/mL in PBS).
Manually pass the BMPS solution through channels of AFM-Chip using polyethylene tubes.
Incubate silanized glass surfaces with BMPS for 30 min at 23°C.
Dilute concentrated EpCAM, PSMA, and PSA antibody solutions to 10 μg/mL using PBS in Eppendorf tubes under a biosafety cabinet.
Mix the diluted solution using a vortex mixer for 5 seconds.
Repeat steps 6 and 7 three times, each time using separate AFM-Chips to immobilize anti-EpCAM, anti-PSMA, and anti-PSA antibodies.
Fill a glass syringe with 100 μL of antibody solution per AFM-Chip.
Manually pass the antibody solution through the channels of the AFM-Chip using polyethylene tubes.
Incubate the maleimide-activated surfaces for 45 minutes at 23°C.
Prepare a 1% (v/v) BSA solution in PBS in a 50 mL centrifuge tube.
Transfer the BSA solution to a 100 μL syringe.
Manually pass the BSA solution through AFM-Chip channels using polyethylene tubes.
Allow for 20 min to block non-specific binding sites on microfluidic channel surfaces.
Manually pass 1 mg NHS-fluorescein in 400 μl of DMF through AFM-Chip channels using a syringe.
Incubate the solution in the dark at 23°C for 60 minutes.
Manually flush the channels with 100 μL PBS using a syringe to remove unbound dyes.
Detach the glass substrate from the PDMS and immerse them in Petri dishes containing dye-free PBS.
Carry out imaging of glass slides with inverted fluorescence microscope using a FITC filter cube and through a 10× air objective.
Calculate the corrected total fluorescence of images following an algorithm that scales and shifts each pixel value to match its mean and standard deviation to those of target images (corrected).
Use a G’MIC color transfer filter to transfer the color characteristics of one image to another in processing the fluorescence images.
Analyze images in ImageJ to calculate the corrected total fluorescence of images using IntDen = (Area) × (MGVSample).
Calculate the corrected total fluorescence (CTF) using CTF = IntDen − (Area × MGVBackground) = (Area) × (MGVSample − MGVBackground).
Obtain immunization against blood-borne diseases, including Hepatitis B and Tetanus.
Obtain IRB ethical approvals from your institution and the collaborating hospital.
Get signed consents from volunteering human subjects after explaining the study.
Collect blood samples in EDTA tubes within 5-6 h of collection.
Place EDTA tubes on a digital rocker at slow mode during cell capture experiments.
Transfer 1 mL of whole blood from EDTA tubes into disposable plastic syringes under a biosafety cabinet using a disposable needle.
Remove any trapped air bubbles in the syringes.
Connect polyethylene tubes to the syringe.
Inject the blood slowly through the connected tubes until it reaches the other end.
Place antibody activated AFM-Chips on a leveled stage.
Mount the syringes to a syringe pump.
Connect the syringes to the AFM-Chips using polyethylene tubes.
Connect the exit ports of the AFM-Chips to a waste container through polyethylene tubes.
Adjust the flow rate of the syringe pump to 20 μL/min.
Inject blood completely into microfluidic channels.
Replace empty blood syringes with glass syringes filled with 100 μL of PBS.
Wash channels at 20 μL/min for 5–10 minutes to remove blood and unattached cells from the channels.
Replace empty PBS syringes with glass syringes filled with 100 μL of anti-PSMA antibodies conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (green).
Pass antibodies through channels at 20 μL/min for 5–10 minutes.
Allow incubation in dark for 20 minutes to immunostain captured CTCs.
Wash the channels with 100 μL of PBS at 20 μL/min for 5–10 minutes to remove excess staining antibodies.
Repeat steps for purity evaluation using anti-CD45 antibodies conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (red).
Immunostain nonspecifically bound white blood cells (WBCs).
Mix different staining antibodies as needed for simultaneous staining of various cell types.
Follow with fluorescence imaging of stained cells.
Manually count captured CTCs using an inverted fluorescence microscope in the dark with FITC filter cube and 20× air objectives.
Count nonspecifically bound WBCs using an inverted fluorescence microscope in the dark with TRITC filter cube and 20× air objective.
Calculate the purity of the device as the ratio of captured CTCs to the total number of bound cells including WBCs.
Perform AFM measurements using a commercially available system such as LS-AFM from AFM Workshop.

Ideally, pair the AFM with an inverted fluorescence microscope and enclose it in a vibration isolation environment for identification of immunomarked CTCs and sound absorption during force measurements.
Slowly peel off the PDMS in the AFM-Chips.
Transfer the glass slides with immunostained captured CTCs onto AFM stage for their nanomechanical characterization.
Use a custom-made PDMS gasket as the "AFM liquid cell" to hold the cell medium in the glass slides.
Mount a 6 μm-diameter colloidal tip with a nominal spring constant of 0.06 N/m on AFM liquid tip holder.
Determine the cantilever spring constants from the power spectral density of the thermal noise fluctuations.
Define a clean (cell-free) area on the glass surface and approach the tip to engage with the surface.
Calibrate the sensitivity of the photodiode by indenting the tip against the glass surface.
Disengage the tip and position it above the center of a single captured intact CTC using the AFM integrated camera.
Approach the tip to engage with the cell surface.
Perform the force measurements either in single force mode or in force volume mode.
In the latter, repeat the tip approach-retraction process over a 10 μm² cell surface area at a resolution of 8 × 8 pixels.
Set the trigger force to 6–12 nN.
Set the tip approach and retraction velocities to 4 μm/s.
Define a proper trigger force by which cells will be pushed against the tip following initial tip-cell surface contact.
Keep the trigger force constant during subsequent AFM measurements.
Fix captured CTCs and WBCs using 4% (v/v) paraformaldehyde for 10 min.
Permeabilize fixed cells using 0.25% (v/v) Triton X-10 for 10 min.
Immunostain the cells for DAPI (blue) and CK (red) in the dark for 30 min.
Verify captured CTCs are DAPI+/CK+/EpCAM+ with an inverted fluorescence microscope.
Identify WBCs as DAPI+/CD45+/EpCAM-.
Define the maximum adhesion forces from each data point in retraction curves.
Assign as minima if they are less than their 5 nearest points to the right and left.
Choose a cut-off force value of 10 pN due to experimental noise during measurements.
Use a trapezoidal integral to calculate the work of detachment area between the zero-force line and the retraction curve.
Apply the classical Hertz model of contact mechanics for elasticity measurements.
Choose a fit range of 100 nm when applying the model.
Set the Poisson ratio of the cell to 0.5 assuming incompressibility.
